HONORING DOLORES HUERTA
(Mr. GARCÍA of Illinois was recognized to address the House for 5 minutes.)
Mr. GARCÍA of Illinois. Mr. Speaker,
today I rise in recognition of a trailblazing feminist, a giant of the labor
and civil rights movement, and an icon
in the Mexican-American history of
this country, Dolores Huerta.
For over seven decades, Dolores
Huerta fought tirelessly for the voiceless—organizing marginalized communities for economic, political, and social justice.

In 1962, she helped found what is
known as the United Farm Workers,
serving as the vice president until 1999
and playing a central role as the
union’s lead negotiator, securing labor
contracts and legislative victories.
It is where she first gave us the rallying cry that echoes in our hearts forever, ‘‘Si, se puede,’’ meaning ‘‘Yes, we
can,’’ because, for Dolores, no obstacle
was too great and no hope was out of
reach.
And through the Dolores Huerta
Foundation, she trained grassroots
leaders and inspired generations to
stand up and speak out.
I am forever grateful for her friendship and for her support when I ran for
mayor of Chicago in 2015. Walking the
campaign trail with Dolores was a
learning experience. She was persuasive and could lighten up every conversation with voters.
When the painful revelations of the
abuse she endured at the hands of
Cesar Chavez came to light, our hearts
broke for the quiet burden she carried
for decades.
Yet, in true Dolores fashion, she refused to let pain define her. Instead,
she continued to transform heartache
into a powerful, unstoppable force for
change.
Dolores Huerta will be remembered
for her unbreakable spirit and tireless
fight for working people.
Mr. Speaker, may my dear friend rest
in power.
HONORING 40 YEARS OF THE ICIRR

Mr. GARCÍA of Illinois. Mr. Speaker,
I stand today to honor the work that
the Illinois Coalition for Immigrant
and Refugee Rights, ICIRR, has done
for 40 years.
Since 1986, ICIRR has been dedicated
to promoting the rights of immigrants
and refugees and to bring them into
full participation in civic, cultural, social, and political life.
ICIRR has advocated and helped pass
pro-immigrant legislation in Illinois,

establishing the first permanent line
item in the State budget dedicated to
immigrant services in the country.
It has helped pass legislation to provide in-State tuition for undocumented
students, created scholarships for immigrant youth pursuing higher education, and helped create the Governor’s Office of New Americans in the
Governor’s office and the city of Chicago.
More than 100,000 immigrants have
been able to prepare applications for
citizenship thanks to ICIRR’s workshops. More than half a million individuals and families have had access to
safety-net services thanks to the organization’s focus on the well-being of
people, including many of my constituents.
And ICIRR successfully fought the
opening of seven for-profit immigration prisons in Illinois and Indiana.
During Operation Midway Blitz,
when our communities were being terrorized by Federal immigration agents,
ICIRR trained community members on
how to defend their rights and served
as a central organizing and rapid response force, setting a national example to resist Trump’s fascism.
My team and I have been honored to
have ICIRR as a key partner, organizing citizenship workshops, Know
Your Rights trainings, and standing for
immigrants in the face of Trump’s
cruel policies.
For 40 years, ICIRR and their work
have strengthened our community with
the vision for how to ensure a more equitable society rooted in dignity and
respect for all.
Mr. Speaker, I thank ICIRR for their
vital work.
The SPEAKER pro tempore. Members are reminded to refrain from engaging in personalities toward the
President.

RECOGNIZING THE SERVICE OF
BOB EVNEN
(Mr. BACON of Nebraska was recognized to address the House for 5 minutes.)
Mr. BACON. Mr. Speaker, I rise to
recognize and honor a dedicated public
servant who has led our State with integrity, vision, and effectiveness: Nebraska’s 27th Secretary of State, Bob
Evnen.
Since taking office in January 2019,
Secretary Evnen has worked to
strengthen our elections, support our
economy, and represent Nebraska
around the world.
On elections, Bob authored a bill instituting Nebraska’s voter ID law, expanded hand-counted postelection audits of every Statewide election, and
opened testing processes to public observers to increase transparency. He
has also worked to secure ballot drop
boxes, all with the goal of giving Nebraskans confidence in their elections.
Secretary Evnen also served as a
leader in Nebraska’s business community. By modernizing State filing systems, cutting red tape, and eliminating
unnecessary fees, his office made it
easier and less expensive for entrepreneurs to start, operate, and grow
their businesses in Nebraska.
As Nebraska’s Ambassador abroad,
Bob showcased our State’s world-class
agricultural products, especially our
premium corn and beef. His trade missions to Taiwan, Israel, Bulgaria,
Egypt, and beyond opened international markets for our farmers and
ranchers.
Whether securing our elections, promoting our agriculture, modernizing
State services, or serving on the Board
of Pardons, Bob brought the same diligence to the office that marked his 40year legal career and his service on the
State of Board Education.
Along with his wife, Debra; his children; and his grandchildren, Secretary
Evnen embodies Nebraska values. On
behalf of our State, I thank Secretary
Evnen for his outstanding service and
commitment to Nebraska.

If you look at what’s happened with

and at least 866 have been wounded.
These are not just numbers. These are
Americans who put on a uniform,
served their country, and had families

HONORING THE LIFE OF RICHARD
ASARO
(Mr. LAWLER of New York was recognized to address the House for 5 minutes.)
Mr. LAWLER. Mr. Speaker, I rise
today to honor the life of Richard
Asaro, a lifelong resident of Mount
Kisco who passed away this past October at the age of 69.
For nearly seven decades, Richard
called Mount Kisco home and dedicated
his life to his family, his business, and
the community he loved. Since 1982, he
owned and operated Mount Kisco Refrigeration, building a family business
that continues today through his son.
Richard’s commitment to his community extended well beyond his work.
For more than 48 years, he served as a
volunteer firefighter with Union Hook
and Ladder Company, where he also
served as president. A proud Eagle
Scout, Richard lived by the principle of
always being ready to help others, and
he never hesitated to lend a hand to
someone in need.
Above all, Richard will be remembered for his generosity, his devotion
to his family, and the countless ways
he gave back to the town he loved.
My thoughts and prayers are with his
wife, Nancy; his children and grandson;
and all who knew and loved him. May
he rest in peace.

HONORING THE LIFE OF MICHAEL SHINE

Mr. LAWLER. Mr. Speaker, I rise
today to honor the life of Michael
Shine, who passed away peacefully surrounded by his family on October 25 at
the age of 98.
Born in County Roscommon, Ireland,
Michael immigrated to New York at
the age of 21, beginning a life defined
by hard work, service, and devotion to
family. He proudly served as a sergeant
in the United States Army during the
Korean war, earning the Bronze Star,
and later served with the New York
City Police Department.
Michael went on to build a successful
career as a self-employed contractor,
becoming well known throughout
Rockland County for his craftsmanship.
No matter how far life took him, he
never lost his connection to his Irish
roots, making more than 100 trips back
to Ireland to remain close to the family and heritage he loved. Michael’s life
was a testament to the importance of
family, service, and remembering
where you came from.
My thoughts are with his family, his
children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and all who knew and loved
him. He will be deeply missed.

BANNING STOCK TRADING BY
ELECTED OFFICIALS
(Mr. MAGAZINER of Rhode Island was
recognized to address the House for 5
minutes.)
Mr. MAGAZINER. Mr. Speaker, last
week, the American people spoke loud
and clear. They want an end to the corruption that has ruined Washington.
We have a mandate for change, and
that starts with finally, at long last,
banning Members of Congress and the
President from trading stocks. The
American people know that when elected officials are allowed to trade off of
inside information, when they get rich
off of their positions, they aren’t going
to do what is best for the country.
The time has come. Our next Speaker, HAKEEM JEFFRIES, has committed
to putting it on the floor next year, as
has Leader SCHUMER in the Senate.
More than 100 candidates for Congress ran television ads calling for a
congressional stock trading ban in the
last election. Most importantly, the
American people are demanding that
we do this. The time has come.
This bill must be strong. It must
fully ban buying, owning, and selling
individual stocks altogether, and it
must include the President of the
United States, whose net worth has
grown by $3 billion in the last 2 years
and who has traded more stocks than
every Member of Congress combined.
We have a good bill ready to go to
end this practice once and for all, a bill
that I worked on last year with Ranking Member JOE MORELLE, Representatives OCASIO-CORTEZ and JAYAPAL, and
our Republican partners CHIP ROY and
BRIAN FITZPATRICK, among many others. Under the leadership of Speaker
JEFFRIES, we will be ready to move
swiftly and deliver.
Banning stock trading in Congress
and the White House must be part of a
larger effort to root out corruption
here in Washington. The corruption
leads politicians to turn a blind eye at
corporate greed that drives up prices
and makes life unaffordable. The
American people have waited long
enough. It is time.

GEORGIA PORTS
(Mr. CARTER of Georgia was recognized to address the House for 5 minutes.)
Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Madam
Speaker, I rise today to recognize the
great economic impact of the Georgia
ports. Georgia ports’ economic impact
grew by 4 percent in 2025, an increase of
$7 billion compared to the previous
year. The ports now generate $181 billion in total annual sales and supports
over 605,000 full-time and part-time
jobs across the State of Georgia.
Port-related activity accounts for 12
percent of Georgia’s total economic
output. Twelve percent means nearly
one in every eight jobs in Georgia is
tied to our ports. Between 2021 and
2025, employment supported by port activity grew by more than 44,500 jobs,
yielding $44 billion in income for Georgia workers.
The Georgia Ports Authority continues to invest in the future through a
$5 billion infrastructure plan, including
new berths at the Port of Savannah
and in Brunswick. These ports remain
a vital engine of opportunity for the
entire First District and our State.

RECOGNIZING INTERNATIONAL
CJD AWARENESS DAY
(Mr. VALADAO asked and was given
permission to address the House for 1
minute and to revise and extend his remarks.)
Mr. VALADAO. Mr. Speaker, this
Thursday is International CreutzfeldtJakob Disease, or CJD, Awareness Day.
I will take a moment to raise awareness about this rare brain disease. CJD
causes a rapid decline in a person’s cognitive health and often leads to death
within a few months or 1 year following the onset of symptoms. While
there are approximately 600 new cases
in the United States each year, this
condition sadly does not have a cure.
In 2018, I was personally impacted by
the loss of a dear friend and mentor,
the former mayor of Bakersfield and
founder of Hall Ambulance Service,
Harvey L. Hall.
Harvey Hall was a compassionate
man with great love for life, his family,
the Central Valley, and the Nation. He
was also a beloved member of our community and the longest-serving mayor
in Bakersfield history.
Sadly, Mayor Hall lost his life just 2
weeks after his CJD diagnosis. While
we don’t have a cure for this disease,
raising awareness for CJD brings us
closer to breakthroughs in treatments,
faster diagnostics, and vital support
that caregivers need.
Together, we can bring hope to those
living with this devastating disease
and the families who have lost loved
ones to CJD.
f

Mr. GRIFFITH. Mr. Speaker, I yield

The Rules Committee met last night
and favorably reported a rule providing
for consideration of one measure, the
Retirement Fairness for Charities and
Educational Institutions Act of 2025.
House Resolution 1650 provides for
consideration of H.R. 1013, the Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act of 2025, under
a closed rule. The rule provides for 1
hour of general debate equally divided
and controlled by the chair and ranking minority member of the Committee
on Financial Services or their respective designees and provides for one motion to recommit.
H.R. 1013 is a bill trying to make retirement more secure for a huge swath
of the population who work at nonprofit organizations, including at hospitals and public schools.
Millions of public schoolteachers,
nurses, some first responders, and charity employees depend on section 403(b)
tax-sheltered annuity plans for their
retirement. These 403(b) plans were set
up to provide a way for nonprofits to
offer retirement benefits and compete
with 401(k) plans and private pensions.
However, 403(b) plans have been left
behind and have had more restrictive
rules around which investments those
institutionally sponsored plan managers are allowed to make. The bill allows these plans the option of investing
in collective investment trusts if they
so choose.
Collective investment trusts are
similar to mutual funds but have a
lower cost to its investors. To clarify,
these products are sold to retirement
plans and not to individual retail investors. These types of investment decisions are routinely made under the
401(k) plans, and there is no reason for
nonprofit workers to be hindered in
their retirement returns only because
these plans aren’t available to them.

VerDate Sep 11 2014

05:33 Nov 11, 2026

H6123

CONGRESSIONAL RECORD — HOUSE

Jkt 079060

The types of investments that we are
talking about under this bill are already an option for 401(k) beneficiaries
and for Federal employee retirement
accounts.
I have heard some Members on the
other side of the aisle act like each retirement plan is forced to invest in collective investment trusts. That is not
so. I would also remind them that each
plan manager still has to apply fiduciary rules to whatever investment decisions they make for plan beneficiaries.
I get the concern. My mother, who
has since passed away, was a public
schoolteacher. She was a single parent
who slept on a couch in our front room
so that my sister and I could each have
our own bedrooms, so I understand the
importance of protecting the retirement of teachers and nonprofit employees. This bill does that.
What this bill looks to do is to allow
for more competition in the retirement
investment market, which will hopefully lead to more plans investing in
pools with lower fees and higher returns that ultimately make it more
likely for retirees to get bigger payouts.
I understand the skepticism when we
are looking at a distinct class of retirees. I would emphasize again, there are
rules around how retirement plan managers are required to evaluate investments for each plan.
Really, what Republicans are aiming
to do with this bill is to increase retirement parity and expand access to
retirement benefits to people who work
for nonprofits or who are schoolteachers.
I hope all Members of this House support the passage of this rule and the
underlying bill. I urge a ‘‘yes’’ vote.

Section 2(c) provides that ‘‘the constitutional powers of the President as Commander-in-Chief to introduce United States
Armed Forces into hostilities, or into situations where imminent involvement in hostilities is clearly indicated by the circumstances, are exercised only pursuant to
(1) a declaration of war, (2) specific statutory
authorization, or (3) a national emergency
created by attack upon the United States,
its territories or possessions, or its armed
forces.’’
The War Powers Resolution further expressly provides that nothing contained
therein ‘‘shall be construed as granting any
authority to the President’’ to introduce
United States Armed Forces into hostilities
which the President would not otherwise
possess in the absence of the Resolution. Accordingly, the reporting and termination
procedures subsequently established by the
Resolution do not themselves constitute affirmative statutory authorization to commence hostilities; rather, the introduction of
United States Armed Forces into hostilities
must rest upon one of the authorities or circumstances identified in section 2(c) in order
for a conflict to be considered lawful.

THANKING EMPORIA, KANSAS
(Mr. SCHMIDT asked and was given
permission to address the House for 1
minute and to revise and extend his remarks.)
Mr. SCHMIDT. Mr. Speaker, I rise
today to honor Emporia, Kansas, the
founding city of Veterans Day.
In 1953, local resident Alvin J. King,
moved by the loss of his nephew in
World War II, believed our Nation
should honor all veterans, not only
those who served in the World War I.
That November 11, Emporia hosted
the first All Veterans Day, setting an
example for our Nation.
Then-Congressman Ed Rees of Emporia carried Mr. King’s vision to Washington.
In 1954, President Dwight D. Eisenhower, another notable Kansan, signed
the bill establishing Veterans Day.
This week, the Lyon County History
Center in Emporia unveiled a plaque
honoring Alvin King’s leadership in the
renaming of Armistice Day as Veterans
Day. The plaque will be located at the
site of Mr. King’s former shoe store on
Commercial Street in downtown Emporia, a fitting tribute to the man whose
vision helped create our national tradition.
Congress by concurrent resolution in
2003 recognized Emporia’s role, and its
legacy lives on every November 11.
On this eve of Veterans Day, I thank
Emporia and its citizens for their leadership and extend my deepest gratitude
to all of America’s veterans. We owe
them a debt of gratitude that can never
be fully repaid.

make District Six better.

this House running, I thank you as

I have had the privilege of serving in

came to Congress in 1993 as the youngest Member of the 103rd Congress. I departed after the 104th Congress in 1997
following the ruling of the Court that
declared the district that I represented
to be an unconstitutional racial gerrymander.
I then returned to Congress 28 years
later in 2025 as a part of the 119th Congress, this Congress. I will depart again
soon because of another Court ruling
that the district that I currently represent is an unconstitutional racial
gerrymander.

say that I have never served a single
day in this body without a Federal lawsuit to dismantle the district that I
represent hanging over my head. Both

the very right that is so basic, to represent his constituents.

Garfield, who said on this floor: Mr.
Speaker, it is too early to allow a
Negro to be seated in this body. Let’s
keep the seat vacant, and let’s save
$5,000. They then sent Menard back to
Louisiana.

Second Congressional District, he was
never seated.

the 20th President of the United States

HONORING THE LIFE AND LEGACY
OF SAMUEL BENJAMIN HOLLIS
(Under the Speaker’s announced policy of January 3, 2025, Mr. CARTER of

as the designee of the majority leader.)
Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize Samuel
Benjamin Hollis of Okatie, South Carolina. Hollis is a decorated World War II
veteran who passed away July 7 at the
age of 100.
Born in Mayfield, Georgia, Sam answered the call to serve at just 17, entering the United States Army immediately after high school. He served
honorably as a sergeant in the European theater from 1943 to 1945.
After the war, Sam earned degrees
from the University of Georgia and the
Woodrow Wilson School of Law and became a certified public accountant.
Sam devoted his career to public
service as regional counsel for the
United States Government, earning respect for his integrity and wisdom.
Sam is survived by his wife, Mary;
his daughters, Mel Evans and Kathryn
Hollis Peters; and many other loving
relatives.
Sam lived through a century of
change, helping shape history through
his service to God, country, and family.

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize Amicalola
Falls for being named Georgia’s top
natural spiritual home.
Thousands of Georgians recently
ranked the State park as Georgia’s
number one most iconic natural feature. The results ranked Amicalola
against destinations along the coast, in
the mountains, and across the State’s
distinctive natural landscapes.
The State park has become beloved
due to its natural splendor and cultural

VerDate Sep 11 2014

07:18 Nov 11, 2026

Jkt 079060

significance to the people of Georgia.
The park’s important connection to
the Appalachian Trail southern trailhead has made the State park a national hotspot for tourists from around
the country.
Georgia’s natural beauty is some of
the finest in the Nation, and I commend the State park system for the
fine work they have done in preserving
Georgia’s beauty. It is my hope that
Amicalola Falls will continue to serve
as an example of Georgia’s beauty for
generations to come.
RECOGNIZING ALFRED MCGUIRE

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize Alfred
McGuire for his 15 years of service to
the Woodville-Tompkins Technical and
Career High School.
Mr. McGuire served 15 years as the
school’s principal and has made a profound impact on the local community
and student body. He will be remembered for his kindness, generosity, and
unwavering dedication to the wellbeing of staff and students.
Mr. McGuire is the type of principal
who truly leaves an impact, knowing
every student and staff member’s name
and taking time out of his schedule to
remember the little moments that
matter.
Mr. McGuire will be taking on a new
district role and will serve as the new
executive director of college and career
readiness for the Savannah-Chatham
County Public School System. He will
no doubt continue to be a shining light
to others within the district, making a
lasting impact on students’ lives.
RECOGNIZING CARY HILL

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize and congratulate Officer Cary Hill for being
named the police chief of Richmond
Hill.
Throughout his career, Officer Hill
has shown dedication for serving and
protecting his community. He had been
serving as police chief on an interim

keeping the city safe. Now he will serve
as the official police chief in a more
complete capacity.

shines through every day as he works
to keep Richmond Hill safe and secure.
I hope that all Georgians can follow his
example and show love and dedication
to their communities.
Mr. Speaker, I extend my deepest
congratulations to Officer Cary Hill. I
know Richmond Hill will remain safe
under his watch.

HAPPY 139TH ANNIVERSARY TO TYBEE ISLAND

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize and congratulate Tybee Island on its 139th anniversary of incorporation.
Tybee Island has been a mainstay of
Savannah, both in history and tourism
for decades, and brought joy to the
residents of the island and beyond.
Tybee Island was named after the
Yuchi word for ‘‘salt’’ because of the
seawater that draws visitors from all
over the country.
Tybee is at the heart of Savannah
tourism, welcoming roughly 2 million
visitors a year. It truly cements Savannah as the ‘‘Hostess City of the South’’
and represents the best and the most
beautiful of the district.
Our State is very proud to call Tybee
a part of Georgia.
Mr. Speaker, I wish Tybee a very
happy 139th anniversary and extend my
best wishes and gratitude to the island,
the people who help it run, and the people who call it home.
RECOGNIZING ATLANTA AREA ROTARY CLUB

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize the Atlanta Area Rotary Club and congratulate them on their centennial celebration.
The rotary club serves as a place to
give back to your community and has

Some issues they are especially interested in are literacy as well as stopping
polio.
Through coin collections, walks, auctions, and countless other community
outreach opportunities, this group has
shown their dedication to Georgia and
to their fellow man.
After 100 years, the Atlanta Area Rotary Club has become an integral part
of the community, and I sincerely congratulate them on this occasion as well
as the countless people they have been
able to help.
Mr. Speaker, I hope that all of Georgia sees this example and strives to
emulate the selflessness and service
that this group demonstrates as each
year passes.

RECOGNIZING SAVANNAH/HILTON HEAD
INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise to recognize the Savannah/
Hilton Head International Airport and
congratulate them on being named the
number one airport in the United
States for the seventh year.
This airport has served as a major
gateway for Savannah, Hilton Head,
and the surrounding area since the
first commercial flight in 1950.
Since then, it has been a mainstay in
connecting people worldwide whether
they are visiting our beautiful district
or representing it elsewhere.
The Savannah/Hilton Head airport
boasts over 50 nonstop departures daily
served by 11 different airlines.
Mr. Speaker, I congratulate the ladies and gentlemen that make this airport run so smoothly and thank them
for being a true shining beacon of
southern hospitality. They truly represent some of the best Georgia has to
offer. I wish them nothing but the best
in their continued endeavors.

RECOGNIZING DOUG WEATHERS

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize my good
friend, Mr. Doug Weathers, and congratulate him on turning 95.
Doug Weathers started at WTOC just
2 weeks after its creation in 1954, starting as a film splicer. Eventually, he
worked his way up, going from there to
becoming a news anchor, to finally becoming the Vice President of News.
Weathers was known for his community-focused approach to the news,
often featuring stories about large
vegetables grown by local farmers and
big fish that were caught.
Viewers love Weathers for his hometown approach and his popularity
never wavered throughout his career.
Doug Weathers has spent his life serving and keeping the people of Savannah
informed, all the while remaining true
to his roots.
Mr. Speaker, I wish a happy birthday
to my friend, the Savannah legend, and
thank him for all of his years of service. I congratulate Doug on a stellar
career and happy birthday.

RECOGNIZING KEN QUINN

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize my friend,
Ken Quinn, who has been with the Department of War’s global privately

RECOGNIZING BACON PARK MUNICIPAL GOLF
COURSE

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise to recognize the Bacon Park
Municipal Golf Course centennial celebration and congratulate them on 100
years of operation in Savannah, Georgia.
Opening in 1926, this golf course was
named after Chatham County Commissioner Judge Oliver T. Bacon.
706 acres were set aside for the golf
course for the promotion of residents’
health, recreation, and enjoyment.
Bacon Park Golf Course has provided
a place for Savannah residents and
guests alike to enjoy nature and spend
time with their friends, colleagues, and
loved ones and is a beloved addition to
Savannah.
In addition to the sense of community it brings, the golf course is a living piece of Georgia history. I hope
that this celebration inspires Georgians to get outside and enjoy recreation in our beautiful State.
Mr. Speaker, I again congratulate
Bacon Park Municipal Golf Course and
I hope that there are many more years
of operation to come.

HONORING FREDERICK BARBER

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to honor the life of Fred
Barber, a lifelong Georgia resident who
passed away this past September.
Mr. Barber spent his whole life in the
service of others, becoming a respected
pharmacist, a community servant, and
friend to countless people who call
Georgia home.
Mr. Barber owned and operated Barber’s Pharmacy for 50 years and earned

E:\CR\FM\K10NO7.048

H6144

quite the reputation for honesty and
customer service.
He was a member of the Georgia
State Board of Pharmacy for 10 years,
and he was also a member of the Georgia Pharmaceutical Association, having served on the board of directors.
Mr. Barber was an incredibly active
member of his community and served
on the board of several notable and
local organizations, like his local
Chamber of Commerce and Rotary
Club.
In his free time, Mr. Barber took
great joy in hunting, football, and
spending time with his family.
Mr. Barber was a star football player
at the University of Georgia and actually played on one of Vince Dooley’s
first football teams. He was a great
athlete.
Mr. Barber is survived by his wife of
58 years, Julie Musgrove, as well as
plethora of children and grandchildren,
who shall all miss him dearly.
RECOGNIZING TOMMY SMITH

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I recognize and honor the life of
Tommy Smith, who served as a Georgia State Representative for 34 years.
Mr. Smith is remembered in the
Georgia General Assembly for his leadership, dedication, and commitment to
his State. He started at an early age as
a peanut farmer with his grandfather
and used that experience to better connect with his Georgia constituents. He
credited those lessons with preparing
him for his life in politics.
He is remembered by his sister, stepsister, nieces, and a great many other
people who carry on his story for generations to come.
Tommy Smith was a great example
of a Georgian coming from humble
farmer beginnings and building his way
up to serving the community that
raised him.
I hope that Georgians hear his story
and are inspired by him.
Mr. Speaker, I offer my deepest condolences as well as my respect for
Tommy Smith, who I served with in
the Georgia State legislature, to his
family and loved ones.

RECOGNIZING BYRON POWERS

Mr. CARTER of Georgia. Mr. Speaker, I rise today to recognize and congratulate Byron Powers on his retirement from ministry alongside his wife,
Frankie.
Byron Powers’ first senior pastor assignment came in 1984 at the Lincoln
Church of God. Mr. Powers traveled
from church to church for a few years
until finally settling in Ludowici,
Georgia, and has served there since. He
also became the chaplain for the
Ludowici Police Department not long
after moving to the area.
In 2017, he founded the Long County
Pastors Fellowship, bringing local pastors together and bringing a community of individual committed to compassion, selflessness, and service.
Mr. Powers, along with his wife,
Frankie, in addition to his passion for
ministry, also shared a passion for
strengthening marriages, which they
did in the form of marriage workshops.
Mr. Powers and his wife will retire to
Tennessee after serving Georgia for so
many years, and I wish nothing but the
best for the two of them. I hope that
every Georgian can emulate the compassion, love, and joy that Mr. Powers
brought to his community during his
time in ministry.

CHINA

Mr. SCHUMER. Mr. President, despite talking a big game, Trump continues to show a troubling resistance
to confront China on AI and to protect
American national security.
The press reports that Trump was
briefed more than a year ago that
Nvidia’s CEO was having an affair with
a suspected Chinese spy, and Trump
didn’t do anything—anything—about
it. Can you believe that? One of our
most important companies that is involved in national security and the
CEO might be having an affair with a
Chinese spy and Trump did nothing
about it? What a dereliction of duty.
He is supposed to protect America, not
China, not his friends.
Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be
defending our national security. It is
that simple. It is obvious.
Instead, Trump invited Nvidia’s CEO
to join him on a visit to Beijing, took
his advice on granting the PRC access
to some of our most advanced AI chips,
and accepted a $25 million donation
from the company for his golden ballroom.
I have been saying this for years: Our
cutting-edge AI chips are too valuable
to fall into the hands of potential adversaries.
This alarming situation makes it
clear that Congress must now act to
pass critical bipartisan legislation like
the AI OVERWATCH Act, the MATCH
Act, and Chip Security Act to cut off
China’s access to advanced American
technology before it is too late.
Myself and colleagues have been
pushing on this for quite a while, and I
urge my Republican colleagues to come
together with us to pass this legislation while we still can. And I call on
the Trump administration to brief the
Senate and House Intelligence Committees immediately on the PRC’s efforts to spy on Nvidia and other U.S.
AI companies.
We also need answers on Nvidia’s influence campaign and how it affected

HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT

Mr. President, the tantrum Pete
Hegseth threw at the Pentagon this
morning only further weakened Americans’ confidence in his ability to lead
our brave men and women in uniform.
The Senate needs to put Hegseth on
trial and remove him from the Pentagon for his management of this disastrous, illegal war. He must be put on
trial.
This morning, Pete Hegseth had the
audacity to declare a ‘‘historic military victory’’ in Iran. Can you believe
it? What the hell is he talking about?
A gallon of gas costing more than $4
a gallon is not a historic victory.
Iran and its proxies still taking potshots at passing ships 8 months into
the war isn’t a historic victory.
Trying to hide American casualty
numbers from the public certainly
doesn’t scream ‘‘historic victory.’’

arguing that the Vietnam war was

but he is nothing more than a deranged
pundit. He has to go. Hegseth is already trying to hide behind our troops,
falsely claiming that Congress disapproves of our courageous servicemembers, even though we have fought
to bring them home for months.

falls solely on the shoulders of the
Trump
administration’s
disastrous
leadership,
not
on

NATIVE AMERICAN HERITAGE MONTH

Mr. DAINES. Mr. President, this
month is Native American Heritage
Month. It has been a meaningful tradition of mine for the past 14 years in
Congress to celebrate the rich legacy of
Montana’s Tribes, and this month is
particularly meaningful, as I close out
my time in the U.S. Senate.
My interest in Montana’s Tribes
began at a very young age. I grew up in
the Gallatin Valley, back in the 1960s.
In fact, I am a graduate of Longfellow
Elementary School in Bozeman. I was a
proud Bozeman Hawk in my high
school days.
As a child, I lived two doors down
from a member of the Crow Tribe. This
was on South Bozeman, a long time
ago. And he was a code talker during
World War II. His name was Barney Old
Coyote. He was an American hero.
Barney served our country during
World War II by speaking the Crow language in a national ‘‘code talk’’ program. The beautiful complexity of the
Crow language allowed it to be used to
transmit and receive military intelligence without fear of being intercepted. Because of Barney and his fellow code talkers, countless communications were securely sent overseas.
Many American lives were saved.
In fact, in 2015, Barney Old Coyote
was awarded Congress’s most prestigious honor, the Congressional Gold
Medal, along with fellow Crow code
talkers Samson Birdinground, Cyril
Not Afraid, and Henry Old Coyote.
And for a fun fact, as a little grade
school kid in Bozeman, I used to walk
to school with Rachel Old Coyote, the
daughter of Barney Old Coyote, the
cousin of Darrin Old Coyote, who was
once the chairman of the Crow Tribe.
As you can see, my roots in Indian
Country start at an early age and run
deep.
But, today, I would like to reflect on
memories from working with Montana’s Tribes, from the wins we have
had over the years to priorities I hope
my successors will continue after my
departure.
Montana is home to many Tribes, including the Crow, the Cheyenne, the
Blackfeet, the Assiniboine, the Gros
Ventres, the Salish, the Kootenai, the
Pend d’Oreille, the Little Shell, the
Sioux, the Chippewa, and the Cree.
When I was elected to the U.S. House,
back in 2012, as the at-large Member
from Montana, there were 11 federally
recognized Tribes. I made it a priority
to introduce the Little Shell of the
Chippewa Indians Restoration Act,
which granted Federal recognition to
the Little Shell Tribe.
In 2019, after years of work, this bill
passed and the Little Shell were finally
granted the recognition they deserved.
So, today, Montana is the home of 12
federally recognized Tribes, spread

VerDate Sep 11 2014

13:38 Nov 11, 2026

S5387

CONGRESSIONAL RECORD — SENATE

Jkt 079060

across 7 reservations, from Fort Peck
in the east to the Flathead in the west.
It has been my honor to visit each
reservation and my priority to meet
regularly with Tribal leaders and members, both back in Montana or in Washington, DC, to work closely together to
improve the quality of life in Indian
Country, whether it is healthcare, education, resource development, or increasing law and order. Each one of
these communities has helped weave
together a rich tapestry of culture in
my home State into the place that it is
today.
The Battle of Little Bighorn, one of
the most significant battles in Montana history, is one such example. In
fact, this year we commemorate the
150th anniversary. The battle marked a
pivotal moment of the Great Sioux War
and the American Indian Wars. It was
my honor to pass a resolution commemorating and honoring all who
fought so that future generations understand and appreciate the enduring
spirit of our Tribes.
Another example is the legacy of
Blackie Wetzel, who was a fierce champion of his people, a former president of
the National Congress of American Indians, who advocated for Tribes, including in the Oval Office with J.F.K.
In fact, in 1971, Blackie worked with
Coach George Allen to create the
iconic logo that became a powerful
symbol of leadership and excellence
during Washington’s three Super Bowl
victories.
Reflecting back in 2002, Blackie
Wetzel proclaimed:
It made us all so proud to have an Indian
on a big-time team.

After the franchise lost its popular
brand in 2020, Blackie’s son Don Wetzel
met with me to share how important
the logo remained for him, his family,
and many in Indian Country. He wanted to use the logo for the good of Native Americans, especially to raise
awareness of missing and murdered indigenous women. But, instead, the logo
was censored by even the NFL and on
official merchandise.
Since then, I am proud to say that
the league and the team have taken
steps to restore the logo to a place of
honor and prominence. It is certainly a
great source of pride for the Blackfeet
Tribe and all Indian Country.
This same warrior-like spirit is demonstrated through a compelling fact
that many don’t know. Listen to this
compelling fact: Native Americans
serve in the military at the highest
rates in America of any ethnic group.
They are patriotic. They are courageous Americans. They have a warrior
ethos. They serve our country in uniform with distinction and great pride.
As an example of that heritage, in
2020, I was honored to join the special
ceremony renaming the Billings VA
Outpatient Clinic in memory of Dr. Joseph Medicine Crow, a proud World War
II veteran and Crow nation Tribal chief
who earned a Bronze Star and was
awarded the Presidential Medal of
Freedom.

Now, when we say ‘‘fix Social Security’’—let’s just make it clear—I mean
to rescue Social Security, to save Social Security. Social Security is like a
baby which is right now sick and you
are trying to rock it to sleep because
the pain that is being released by that
child may not be heard by people who

What am I describing? The problem
with Social Security right now is that
the trust fund is going insolvent. I will
explain that. In years in which workers
paid more in from their paycheck than
was going out, the surplus was put in
what is called the Social Security trust
fund and put into Treasury bills.
We have been in a situation for a
while where there is more going out
than there is coming in, and the difference between the amount going out
and the amount coming in is being
filled with the surplus of that trust
fund. But that balance in the trust
fund is falling. We are looking at an
hourglass, and the hourglass is draining in the top, and it is coming down to
the bottom. And it is not quite an
hourglass, but if you can make the
hourglass about 51⁄2 years from now,
that is when that trust fund is all
empty on the top; there is no more surplus to supplement the amount coming
in.
At that point, by law—by law—by the
wisdom of Franklin Delano Roosevelt,
who started Social Security, when the
trust fund is empty, the amount going
out, by law, has to fall to equal the
amount coming in. If we wait until the
end, that fall can be a cut of 28.5 percent—almost a third of the benefits
that someone on Social Security is receiving. And it won’t just be those who
are currently receiving; it will be all
those who in the future would receive.
They would also get a 28.5-percent cut.
Now, my good friend JOHN KENNEDY,

there in the future for her—we can reassure her, and we can take care of our
Nation’s fiscal house.
But it takes courage. I admit it takes
courage.
But, I will say, the stars have
aligned. Again, President Trump is all
in. I have got Republican leadership.
We have a bipartisan bill. But we also
have competing bills, say, for example,
from Senator SANDERS and Representative LARSON.
So, Congress, let’s do our job. Let’s
step up to the plate. Choose your metaphor. Lean into it. Let’s do right for
the American people.
If there is anything we learned from
last Tuesday’s election, if people make
promises and don’t keep them, the voters will punish them. Congress has
made a promise to take care of the
American people’s fiscal house that is
represented by Social Security. Let’s
keep that promise.
I yield the floor.

SURVIVOR JUSTICE TAX PREVENTION ACT

Mr. LEE. Mr. President, there was a
time when this country measured its
ambition by what it built. We connected a continent by rail, and we
closed that connection at Promontory
Point in my home State of Utah with
the driving of the Golden Spike. We
raised the Hoover Dam out of the middle of nowhere in the desert. We built
the infrastructure that made America
the most prosperous, upwardly mobile
Nation on planet Earth.
We did these things because we believed the future should be bigger than
the past. Somewhere along the way, we
forgot how to say yes or, better said,
somewhere along the way we developed
a system of laws that made it way too
easy to say no.
Today, a company can spend years
trying to get permission just to build a
powerplant, and a transmission line—
separately from that—can be tied up in
litigation before a single mile of line is
put up. The studies pile up; the legal
bills pile up, but the energy that Americans need desperately never gets produced, and American families pay the
price.
It is a steep price. They see it every
single month in their electric utility
bills. They feel it at the grocery store
where energy costs are reflected in the
price of, well, basically everything on
the shelf. And they are tired of being
told just to be patient.
If we want cheaper energy, we need
more of it. We need more energy on the
grid, and we need it to be reliable.
Now, the White House Council of
Economic Advisers estimates that permitting reform in this legislation could
save the average American household
between $178 and $251 a year just in
electricity alone. And we have a bipartisan agreement to deliver it.

PO 00000

Frm 00009

Fmt 4624

Sfmt 0634

For months, Senator CAPITO, Senator
HEINRICH, Senator WHITEHOUSE, and I
have worked to reach a deal that allows America to build again.
That is not too much to ask, to let
Americans build. We have negotiated
in good faith. We have listened to concerns. We have made difficult compromises. We have strengthened Tribal
consultation provisions and responded
to feedback from stakeholders of different sorts from different backgrounds
all across the country.
This bill will make it easier to
produce American energy and build the
infrastructure that is necessary to deliver it.
And when a massive data center
needs new grid infrastructure, that
data center should pay for it, not the
family down the street from it.
But now at the moment when we are
finally prepared to act, some of the
loudest voices in environmental politics in the United States are demanding that we abandon the agreement.
Now, this is ironic. Some of these
same groups tell us that climate
change demands urgent action. They
demand more renewable energy. But
now, the moment Congress produces bipartisan legislation that would make it
easier to build that kind of energy,
suddenly, they are opposed to it.
Look, environmental laws should
protect the environment. They should
not confer a permanent veto over lawful, legitimate projects that the American people need. We can protect our
natural resources while allowing Americans to build things that our country
needs. That is precisely what this legislation would accomplish.
So my Democratic colleagues face a
choice. They can stand with the bipartisan agreement that their own committee leaders have helped negotiate or
they can surrender that agreement to
outside organizations that have made
opposition their principal business.
They can vote to lower costs for American families or they can vote to preserve the very delays that make everything in this country more expensive.
Look, I recognize that there are sincere, legitimate disagreements about
energy policy, and I think there always
will be. But, at a minimum, we should
be able to agree that Americans deserve timely decisions on lawful
projects, regardless of the means by
which those projects produce electricity or whatever they are producing.
So what is the alternative, if it is not
this bill? Is it another decade of negotiations? Another promise that permitting reform might be just around the
corner?
We have already done the negotiating. We have already made the compromises. Now comes the part where
we keep our word.
America did not become great by
asking permission to remain great. It
became great because Americans were
willing to be bold. They were willing to
build.
The engineers who designed the Hoover Dam were not promised a world

E:\CR\FM\G10NO6.043

S10NOPT1

S5392

without obstacles. The workers who
built it did not wait for perfect conditions. They got to work. We owe it to
the next generation that same ambition.
We have a bipartisan agreement. We
have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity
to make energy more affordable, and,
with it, everything else. Let’s stop
making excuses for why America can’t
build. Let’s give Americans the freedom to build again. I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

Mr. RISCH. Madam President, section 36(b) of the Arms Export Control
Act requires that Congress receive
prior notification of certain proposed
arms sales as defined by that statute.
Upon such notification, the Congress

stipulates that, in the Senate, the notification of proposed sales shall be sent

in environments where GPS signals may be

Annex Item No. vii
(vii) Sensitivity of Technology:
1. The Javelin weapon system is a mediumrange, man portable, shoulder-launched, fireand-forget, anti-tank system for infantry,
scouts, and combat engineers. It may also be
mounted on a variety of platforms including
vehicles, aircraft, and watercraft. The system weighs 49.5 pounds and has a maximum
range in excess of 2,500 meters. The system is
highly lethal against tanks and other systems with conventional and reactive armors.
The system possesses a secondary capability
against bunkers.
2. Javelin’s key technical feature is the use
of fire-and-forget technology that allows the
gunner to fire and immediately relocate or
take cover. Additional special features are
the top attack and/or direct fire modes, an
advanced tandem warhead and imaging infrared seeker, target lock-on before launch,
and soft launch from enclosures or covered
fighting positions. The Javelin missile also
has a minimum smoke motor thus decreasing its detection on the battlefield.
3. The Javelin weapon system is comprised
of two major tactical components, which are
a reusable Lightweight Command Launch
Unit (LWCLU) and a round contained in a
disposable launch tube assembly. The
LWCLU incorporates an integrated daynight sight that provides a target engagement capability in adverse weather and
countermeasure environments. The LWCLU
may also be used in a stand-alone mode for
battlefield surveillance and target detection.
LWCLU’s thermal sight includes an advanced forward-looking infrared sensor. To
facilitate initial loading and subsequent updating of software, all on-board missile software is uploaded via the LWCLU after mating and prior to launch.
4. The missile is autonomously guided to
the target using an imaging infrared seeker
and adaptive correlation tracking algorithms. This allows the gunner to take cover
or reload and engage another target after firing a missile. The missile has an advanced
tandem warhead and can be used in either
the top attack or direct fire modes. An onboard flight computer guides the missile to
the selected target.
5. The highest level of classification of defense articles, components, and services included in this potential sale is SECRET.
6. If a technologically advanced adversary
were to obtain knowledge of the specific
hardware and software elements, the information could be used to develop countermeasures that might reduce system effectiveness or be used in the development of a
system with similar or advanced capabilities.
7. A determination has been made that
Egypt can provide substantially the same degree of protection for the sensitive technology being released as the U.S. Government. This proposed sale is necessary in fur-

POLICY JUSTIFICATION

Australia—Tomahawk Capability
Development
The Government of Australia has requested to buy Theater Mission Planning
Center (TMPC) and associated communications systems; TMPC Mission Planning System (MPS); program management; engineering, training, and logistics services to support the development, procurement, and delivery of the MPS; and other related elements of logistics and program support. The
estimated total cost is $300 million.
This proposed sale supports the foreign
policy and national security objectives of
the United States. Australia is one of our
most important allies and is critical to promoting stability and security in the Indo-Pacific and around the world. Assisting our ally
in developing and maintaining a strong and
ready self-defense capability advances U.S.
national interests.
This proposed sale will improve Australia’s
capability to meet current and future
threats by enhancing its Tomahawk capability, strengthening its ability to deter regional threats, and improving its homeland
defense. Australia will deepen its interoperability with U.S. maritime forces and other
allied forces as well as its ability to contribute to missions of mutual interest. Australia will have no difficulty absorbing these
articles and services into its armed forces.
The proposed sale of this equipment and
support will not alter the basic military balance in the region.
The principal contractors will be BAE Systems, located in San Diego, CA; Tapestry Solutions, located in St. Louis, MO; Peraton,
located in San Jose, CA; and Leidos, located
in Virginia Beach, VA. At this time, the U.S.
Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser
and the contractor.
Implementation of this proposed sale will
not require the assignment of any additional
U.S. Government or contractor representatives to Australia.
There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed
sale.

The AGM–114R2 missile is used against
heavy and light armored targets, thinskinned vehicles, urban structures, bunkers,
caves and personnel. The missile is inertial
measurement unit-based, with a variable
delay fuze, improved safety and reliability.
The highest classification level for release of
the AGM–114R2 is Secret. Software and
firmware documentation, such as data processing, software requirements, source code,
algorithms, height of burst sensor, are not
authorized for disclosure. The highest level
of classified information that could be disclosed by a proposed sale or by testing of the
end item is up to and including Secret. The
highest level that must be disclosed for production, maintenance, or training is up to
and including Secret. Vulnerability data,
countermeasures, vulnerability and susceptibility analyses, and threat definitions are
classified as Secret or Confidential. Detailed
information to include discussions, reports
and

of

classified information associated with the
AGM–114R2 could lead to development of
countermeasures or exploitation of system
vulnerabilities by those obtaining the information.
The Joint Air-to-Ground Missile all up
round, designated AGM–179A, is an air-toground missile (AGM) consisting of a
Hellfire-Romeo (AGM–114R) back-end (i.e.,
propulsion, warhead, and control sections)
mated to a newly designed dual-mode guidance section (GS). The dual-mode GS is a
combination of millimeter wave (MMW) and
semi-active laser (SAL) sensors co-axially
aligned on a steerable gimbal. The combination of MMW and SAL sensors provide improved precision point and fire-and-forget capabilities onto a single munition. This combination allows targeting capability against
fast moving and stationary targets in countermeasure and/or a battlefield intensive environment, and in low cloud ceiling and adverse weather. Firing modes include lock-on
before launch and lock-on after launch. Engagement modes include point designation—
SAL only; target designation—SAL initiated
with MMW engagement completion; active
fire-and-forget laser queuing—MMW initiated with SAL override capability; active
fire and forget—MMW only. Hosting platforms include rotary-wing, select fixed-wing,
wheeled/tracked vehicles, ground-based pedestal launcher, and patrol boats. Lethality
includes tactical armor, boats, bunkers,
buildings, caves, personnel in open, rotary
and slow fixed wing; unmanned aircraft systems, non-tactical vehicles-fast moving. The
MMW is capable of hitting low radar cross
section targets.
The Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS–II) is a design conversion of an
unguided Hydra 2.75–inch rocket with a laser
guidance kit to give it precision-kill capability. As a low-cost weapon, it is intended
as an inexpensive means to destroy targets
while limiting collateral damage in close
combat. The APKWS consists of an APKWS–
II guidance section developed by BAE systems, legacy 2.75–inch MK66 Mod 4 rocket
motor, and a legacy MK151 and MK435/436
warhead/fuze. These guided rockets are

steered to the target by following reflected

The Common Infrared Countermeasure
(CIRCM) is the next-generation lightweight,
laser-based, infrared countermeasure system
for rotary-wing, tilt-rotor, and small fixedwing aircraft across the DoD. CIRCM provides near spherical coverage of the host
platform to defeat infrared (IR)-seeking
threat missiles. CIRCM receives an angular
bearing hand-off from the common missile
warning system, employs a pointing and
tracking system that acquires and tracks
the incoming missile. CIRCM jams the missile by using modulated laser energy, thus
degrading the tracking capability of the missile and causing it to miss the aircraft.
DVEPS provides overmatch by providing
increased situational awareness to the aircrew in Degraded Visual Environment (DVE)
conditions such as brownout, allowing special operations aviation assets to execute
missions in almost any environmental condition. Utilizes using three-dimensional (3D)
imaging technology. DVEPS produces imagery, 3D conformal symbology, and system
alerts to aid pilots in maintaining spatial
awareness during and after transition from
visual meteorological conditions (VMC) to
degraded visual environment (DVE) conditions. DVEPS includes synthetic vision avionics backbone, light detection and ranging,
removable storage device, infrared camera,
power distribution unit, and inertial measurement unit.
The AN/ARC–231A is a software-definable
radio for military aircraft that provides twoway, multi-mode voice and data communications over a 30 Hz to 512 MHz frequency
range. No designated exportable/non-communication security capable version planned.
Support both line-of-sight UHF and VHF
bands with amplitude modulation, frequency
modulation, and SATCOM capabilities including embedded frequency agile modes,
electronic counter-countermeasures antijam waveforms including HAVEWQUICK and
SINCGARS, demand assigned multiple access, integrated waveform. It provides simultaneous, real-time participation in tactical
voice and data communications networks.

The Netherlands—Common Infrared
Countermeasure
The Government of the Netherlands has requested to buy sixteen (16) OT–228/U Common
Infrared Countermeasure systems; and thirty-eight

also be included: U.S. Government technical
assistance with incidental travel; transportation; technical data and reports; ancillary
items; nonrecurring engineering; site surveys; new equipment training; and other related elements of logistics and program support. The estimated total cost is $294 million.
This proposed sale will support the foreign
policy and national security objectives of
the United States by improving the security
of a NATO ally which is an important force
for political stability and economic progress
in Europe.
The proposed sale will modernize the Netherlands’ armed forces, expand its capability
to strengthen homeland defense, and deter
regional threats. This enhanced capability
will contribute to the Netherlands’ military
goals of updating capability while further
enhancing interoperability with the United
States and other allies. The Netherlands will
have no difficulty absorbing these articles
and services into its armed forces.
The proposed sale of this equipment and
support will not alter the basic military balance in the region.
The principal contractor will be Northrop
Grumman, located in Rolling Meadows, IL.
At this time, the U.S. Government is not
aware of any offset agreement proposed in
connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations
between the purchaser and the contractor.

not require the assignment of any additional
U.S. Government or contractor representatives to The Netherlands.
There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed
sale.

CONGRESSIONAL RECORD — SENATE

1. The Common Infrared Countermeasure
(CIRCM) is the next-generation lightweight,
laser-based, infrared countermeasure system
for rotary-wing, tiltrotor, and small fixedwing aircraft across the Department of War.
CIRCM provides near spherical coverage of
the host platform to defeat infrared-seeking
threat missiles. CIRCM receives an angular
bearing hand-off from the Missile Warning
System (Common Missiles Warning System
or Limited Interim Missile Warning System)
and employs a pointing and tracking system
that acquires and tracks the incoming missile. CIRCM jams the missile by using modulated laser energy, thus degrading the tracking capability of the missile and causing it
to miss the aircraft.
2. The AN/APR–39E(V)2 Radar Warning Receiver is a radar threat detection system
that passively detects, categorizes, and
prioritizes radio frequency threats to aircraft, and then provides an audio/visual cue
to aircrew. The AN/APR–39E(V)2 provides a
hIlly digital capability to enhance threat
discrimination in the millimeter wave band
and increases overall system performance
against frequency-agile radio frequency and
active electronically scanned array threat
radars.
3. The highest level of classification of defense articles, components, and services included in this potential sale is SECRET.
4. If a technologically advanced adversary
were to obtain knowledge of the specific
hardware and software elements, the information could be used to develop countermeasures that might reduce system effectiveness or be used in the development of a
system with similar or advanced capabilities.
5. A determination has been made that the
Netherlands can provide substantially the
same degree of protection for the sensitive
technology being released as the U.S. Government. This proposed sale is necessary in
furtherance of the U.S. foreign policy and
national security objectives outlined in the
Policy Justification.
6. All defense articles, technical data, and
services listed in this transmittal have been
authorized for release and export to the Government of The Netherlands.

Jordan—Advanced Precision Kill Weapon
System (APKWS) II
The Government of Jordan has requested
to buy up to one thousand five hundred
(1,500) WGU–59A/B or B/B Single Variant
Block Upgrade (air-to-air, ground-to-air, or
air-to-ground) Advanced Precision Kill
Weapon System II (All-up-rounds or guidance sections). The following non-major defense equipment items will also be included:
launchers; Mk–152 high explosive warheads;
MK66 rocket motors; proximity fuzes; WTU–
1/B practice warheads; inert MK66 rocket
motors; support equipment; publications and
technical documentation; transportation;
U.S. Government and contractor engineering, technical, training, and logistical support services; and other related elements of
logistics and program support. The estimated total cost is $100 million.
This proposed sale will support the foreign
policy and national security objectives of
the United States by helping to improve the
security of a Major Non-NATO Ally that is
an important force for political stability and
economic progress in the Middle East.
The proposed sale will improve Jordan’s
capability to meet current and future
threats by providing enhancement to its air
defense capability in support of the Middle
East Air Defense pillar of the Regional Security Construct. The acquisition of additional
APKWS II guided rockets will increase Jordan’s capacity to defend itself, allow for the
reduction of sustained U.S. support over
time, and provide increased security for U.S.
military assets stationed in Jordan. Jordan
will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces.
The proposed sale of this equipment and
support will not alter the basic military balance in the region.
The principal contractor will be BAE Systems, Inc., located in Nashua, NH. At this
time, the U.S. Government is not aware of
any offset agreement proposed in connection
with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between
the purchaser and the contractor.
Implementation of this proposed sale will
not require the assignment of any additional
U.S. Government or contractor representatives to Jordan, only additional periodic participation in program and technical reviews
and training and maintenance support.
There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed
sale.

thriving city it is today.
Homewood’s story began on October
29, 1926, when the communities of Edgewood, Rosedale, and Grove Park came
together to form a new city in Shades
Valley, just south of Red Mountain and
neighboring Birmingham. Their decision reflected a shared commitment to
building a community that could serve
its residents and provide a strong foundation for future generations.
Over the decades, Homewood has
grown and evolved while maintaining
the distinct character that makes it
such a treasured part of the Birmingham metropolitan area. The city’s
neighborhoods, local businesses, parks,
and public spaces reflect a deep sense
of belonging and a commitment to preserving the qualities that make a community feel like home.
Education has been an important
part of that legacy. In 1970, Homewood
established its own independent school
system, demonstrating the community’s commitment to investing in its
children. Today, Homewood’s schools
continue to play an essential role in
preparing the next generation for success and giving them the tools to succeed and achieve their American
dream.
As we celebrate this milestone, we
recognize that a city’s legacy is measured not simply by years, but also by
the people who give it meaning. We
honor the founders who envisioned
Homewood a century ago, the generations who built and sustained it, and
the residents, educators, public servants, business owners, first responders,
and leaders who continue to contribute
to its success.
I also rise to recognize the importance of preserving Homewood’s history while embracing the opportunities
and responsibilities that lie ahead. The
next century will bring new challenges

REMEMBERING HILMER ‘‘PAUL’’
HERMANN, JR.
∑ Mr. CASSIDY. Madam President, I
rise to pay tribute to Hilmer Hermann,
Jr., known to his family, friends, and
colleagues as Paul. Of all the people
my staff and I have worked with during
my time in the U.S. Senate, I can
think of few others who were as generous, thorough, and patriotic as Paul.
He was born in New Orleans on December 28, 1956, and passed away on
September 23, 2026. The first thing to
know about Paul is that he was a veteran. He signed up for the U.S. Air
Force in 1976 and became a logistics
manager supporting the Air Force’s
Deputy Commander of Resources. He
served for nearly 17 years until taking
medical retirement in 1993.
Upon retirement from the Air Force,
Paul already devoted a substantial portion of his life to serving our country.
He could have ended his public service
there. However, he became involved
with Disabled American Veterans after
one of their representatives successfully helped him file a disability claim
with the U.S. Department of Veterans
Affairs. Paul believed in paying it forward and so began working professionally for DAV.
During his employment with DAV, he
worked as a national service officer
and later as their supervisor in New Orleans from 2002 to 2007. In this work, he
helped other veterans and their families receive the benefits they earned
from the U.S. Department of Veterans
Affairs. This included helping veterans
facing desperate circumstances before,
during, and after Hurricane Katrina.
He also spent time in Nashville working for DAV, including as acting supervisor for their office there.
Despite retiring in 2009, Paul continued to serve veterans, including as
Louisiana department commander and
later department adjutant for DAV.
This is when my staff and I became acquainted with Paul and his passion for
veterans.
My casework team is committed to
helping veterans but relies on community partners to help veterans fill out
VA disability claims and applications
for other forms of assistance. Paul was

available whenever our team needed to
connect a veteran with someone who

meeting, Paul called him about an unrelated matter. When informed about
the veteran in my office, Paul spoke

RECOGNIZING THE LEWISTON
MILL
∑ Mr. RISCH. Madam President, I rise
today to celebrate the Idaho Forest
Group’s Lewiston Mill and its 100 years
of operation. Located adjacent to the
Clearwater River, the Lewiston Mill
has a long history of lumber production and remains a pillar of north central Idaho’s economy.
The Lewiston Mill is part of Idaho
Forest Group, a family-founded business headquartered in Coeur d’Alene
that has grown into one of the Nation’s
largest lumber producers. With seven
sawmills and customers around North
America, Idaho Forest Group produces
more than 1 billion board feet each
year, much of which comes from its
Lewiston facility.
The Lewiston Mill was one of the
first large mills in the Northwest when
it was built in the early 1920s. Spanning 180 acres, the sawmill has evolved
alongside Idaho’s timber industry. Over
a 10-year period that began in 2012, the
mill underwent major improvements,
including two new saw lines and a log
merchandising
and
sorting
line,
strengthening the facility’s ability to
provide high-quality Idaho lumber.
Today, the mill can produce more than
300 million board feet each year.
The Lewiston Mill’s impact extends
well beyond lumber production. It is a
driver of the local economy, provides
jobs, and plays a key role in North
American
lumber
supply
chains.
Through an agreement with Clearwater
Paper, the mill also supplies wood
chips and sawdust that are vital to
paper production at the Lewiston Pulp
Mill.
For 100 years, the Lewiston Mill has
helped put Idaho timber to work. Its
history is a reminder that the forest
products industry remains a cornerstone of the north central Idaho econ-

omy, supporting families, rural communities, and generations of skilled
Idaho workers.
Congratulations to Idaho Forest
Group and the Lewiston Mill on 100
years of operation. I look forward to
the continued success of this essential
mill and its contributions to Idaho.∑

RECOGNIZING RANGE 208
∑ Mr. RISCH. Madam President, Idaho’s veterans made great sacrifices for

Joe Alicea enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps in April 2000, serving for 8
years and completing two deployments.
His extraordinary service earned him
numerous honors, including the Presidential Unit Citation, National Defense
Service Medal, Combat Action Ribbon,
and Rifle and Pistol Expert Badges. He
served as an artillery surveyor and
later to survey information chief, a position typically held by higher ranking
Marines.
In 2025, Joe purchased Diamondback
Shooting Range and renamed it to
Range 208. Tributes to Joe’s service
and the Armed Forces are incorporated
throughout the business. Its logo honors his time in the Marine Corps, depicting the 1st Marine Division’s ‘‘Blue
Diamond’’ and the six stars of Orion’s
Belt and Sword. For Joe, the stars represent both his identity as a warrior
and his mission of building a community of trained, responsible citizens.
Range 208 is the only indoor shooting
range and training academy withing
100 miles of the Lewis-Clark Valley,
and Joe is proud to welcome clients of
all skill levels and experiences. He offers everything from introductory
courses to defensive pistol training, as
well as one-on-one instruction. As a
brother to four sisters and a father to
three daughters, Joe is particularly
committed to helping women develop
the knowledge and confidence to handle firearms safely. Range 208 offers
many classes designed specifically for
women, which have become their largest clientele group.
Joe and his team also believe strongly in giving back to their community.
This October, Range 208 hosted Aim for
Advocacy, a month-long target challenge competition. to find the best
local shot. Proceeds raised during the
event were donated to the Two Rivers
United Child Advocacy Center in
Lewiston, which works with local law
enforcement, child protective services,

STATEMENTS ON INTRODUCED

By Mr. DURBIN (for himself and
Mr. LEE):
S. 5714. A bill to subject professional
baseball clubs to the antitrust laws; to
the Committee on the Judiciary.
Mr. DURBIN. Mr. President, I ask
unanimous consent that the text of the
bill be printed in the RECORD.
There being no objection, the text of
the bill was ordered to be printed in
the RECORD, as follows:
S.5714
Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in
Congress assembled,
SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

S. 5372

VerDate Sep 11 2014

S5415

CONGRESSIONAL RECORD — SENATE

Jkt 079060

This Act may be cited as the ‘‘Competition
in Professional Baseball Act’’.
SEC. 2. PROFESSIONAL BASEBALL SUBJECT TO
ANTITRUST LAWS.
(a) DEFINITION.—In this section, the term

‘‘antitrust laws’’—
(1) has the meaning given the term in subsection (a) of the first section of the Clayton
Act (15 U.S.C. 12); and
(2) includes section 5 of the Federal Trade
Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 45) to the extent
that such section applies to unfair methods
of competition.
(b) REMOVAL OF EXEMPTION.—The conduct,
acts, practices, or agreements of persons in
the business of organized professional baseball are subject to the antitrust laws to the
same extent such conduct, acts, practices or
agreements would be subject to the antitrust
laws if engaged in by persons in any other
professional sports business affecting interstate commerce.
(c) REPEAL.—Section 27 of the Clayton Act
(15 U.S.C. 26b) is repealed.

By Mr. PADILLA (for himself,
Mr. BLUMENTHAL, and Ms. WARREN):
S. 5715. A bill to amend title 38,
United States Code, and the United
States Housing Act of 1937, to make
certain improvements to the supported
housing program for veterans commonly known as ‘‘HUD–VASH’’, and for
other purposes; to the Committee on
Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
Mr. PADILLA. Mr. President, I rise
to introduce the End Veterans Homelessness Act. This legislation seeks to
ensure that more veterans who have
bravely served our country have a roof
over their heads.
On any given night in America, nearly 32,500 veterans experience homelessness. To address this need, Congress
created the HUD-VASH program to distribute
vouchers
to
veterans,
prioritizing those with chronic mental
illnesses or substance use disorders.
Although Congress allocates funding
for 100,000 HUD-VASH vouchers each
year, nearly 24,500 of these vouchers go
unused. This gap in voucher utilization
needlessly results in veterans living
without a home.
The End Veterans Homelessness Act
would modernize the Housing and
Urban Development-Veterans Affairs’
Supportive Housing, (HUD-VASH) program by enhancing efficiency, broadening program eligibility, and increasing oversight.

PO 00000

Frm 00033

Fmt 4624

Sfmt 0634

Under this Act, HUD-VASH eligibility would be expanded to include
unhoused veterans and their families
who are experiencing or at risk of
homelessness and veterans who do not
require intensive supportive services,
while preserving priority for chronically homeless veterans and veterans
with chronic disabilities.
This bill would also allow veterans
currently receiving housing assistance
through other Federal programs to
transfer into HUD-VASH, freeing up
limited housing subsidies for nonveterans in need. In addition, this bill
would allow public housing authorities
to cover certain administrative fees
and require HUD to submit an annual
report to Congress on voucher utilization and barriers to access.
The End Veterans Homelessness Act
is a critical step towards ensuring that
veterans—especially those with chronic
mental illnesses or substance use disorders—can access the help they need.
Veterans deserve to have a home, and
our government has a responsibility to
ensure that its resources are used to
promote veterans’ well-being. By passing this legislation, we can take meaningful action to honor veterans’ service
to our Nation.
I would like to thank Senators WARREN and BLUMENTHAL for coleading this
bill with me, and Representatives
TAKANO, WATERS, and LEVIN for leading
this legislation in the House. I hope
that our colleagues will join us to cut
redtape to make it easier and faster to
house veterans experiencing or at risk
of homelessness and their families.
I look forward to working with my
colleagues to pass the End Veterans
Homelessness Act as swiftly as
possible.
